## Paper

Learning in repeated auctions

## World

auction_house

## Institution

Repeated auction learning protocol.

## Agent type

Learning bidders.

## Theoretical benchmark

Repeated strategic learning can diverge from one-shot auction predictions.

## Learning setup

Repeated independent value draws with policy updates and final-window bid curves.

## Metrics

Learning dynamics, final-window revenue/efficiency/regret, bid shading, convergence behavior.

## Main result

The paper frames repeated auctions as dynamic learning environments where bidder and seller learning can differ from one-shot auction predictions. Use it here as a protocol and metric obligation for repeated auction runs.

## What they prove

Do not treat this card as a single theorem claim. For this repo, it supplies the obligation to evaluate repeated auction learning with dynamic/final-window behavior, regret, revenue, and bid-curve diagnostics.

## What they only simulate

Repeated-auction learning behavior and adaptive bidder/seller dynamics discussed or evaluated in the source text.

## What they do NOT test

This repo's fixed auction world/mind ladder, Resource Island/Public Goods/Labor Market comparisons, and the specific tabular/deep-RL validation protocol used here.

## What we need to reproduce

Treat Auction House as a repeated-learning environment and report final-window summaries plus learned bid curves.

## How our project differs

The paper focuses on repeated auction learning. This repo uses repeated auctions as one world in a larger institution/capability platform.

## Implementation obligations

Fresh private values per episode; bidder observation includes own valuation; final-window summary; bid-curve extraction by valuation bin.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

worlds/auction_house/training.py; outputs/auction_house_full/bid_curves.csv.

## Failure modes to audit

One-shot benchmark claimed as learned convergence; no final-window separation; no bid curve; changing valuation distribution across scenarios without noting it.

## Project code comparison

Compare Learning in repeated auctions to Auction House training outputs. The repo should interpret auction behavior dynamically, not only as one-shot mechanism theory.
